12522.name: Cam Ward
12522.headline: 20/31, 181 yards, one INT in 27-24 loss to Browns
12522.news: Ward completed 20 of 31 passes for 181 yards with no touchdowns and one interception in Tennessee's 27-24 home loss to Cleveland on Oct 25, per Fantasy Footballers. Tony Pollard scored all three Titans touchdowns on the ground. In the Week 6 win at Indianapolis (Oct 18) Ward went 11 of 22 for 102 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Through six games he had 998 passing yards and four TD passes. The Titans face Cincinnati in Week 8 on Nov 1.
12522.take: Ward has four TD passes in seven games and failed to reach 200 passing yards in either of the last two, so he isn't a redraft starter in a 1QB league. Pass protection and a thin receiving group behind Carnell Tate remain the problem. In superflex dynasty, a second-year starter with coaching support still has value, and his price is near its low point, so holding beats selling for a rebuilding team. A Bengals matchup in Week 8 is a possible bounce-back spot for superflex lineups only.

Hold unless a contender pays close to his preseason price.

5967.headline: 25-129 and three TDs with Spears inactive vs. Browns

For a rebuilding dynasty team, sell this 29-year-old in a contract year right now while his box score looks great.

8210.headline: Washington on Week 7 bye; McLaurin injury boosts his role
8210.news: Washington was on bye in Week 7 and hosts Philadelphia on Nov 1. His value comes from volume, not touchdowns, and Philadelphia is a tough Week 8 matchup. In redraft, pick him up where available and consider starting him. In dynasty he's a useful TE2 at 27, and a rebuilding team can sell if a contender pays for the bump in role.

13269.name: Fernando Mendoza
13269.headline: Kubiak sticks with Cousins at Jets; no Mendoza timeline
13269.news: Mendoza did not play in the 35-21 loss to the Rams on Oct 25, the Raiders' fourth straight defeat (3-4). After first saying the staff was "thinking about everything," Klint Kubiak said on Oct 26 that Kirk Cousins will stay the starter for the Nov 1 game at the Jets. He said there is "no controversy" and that Cousins is playing at a very high level. Kubiak said the team has a plan for Mendoza but no timeline for his first start. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler had reported earlier that a Cousins start in Week 8 wasn't a lock, but the team has now committed. Mendoza's only NFL action is still a Week 5 relief appearance (6-of-8, 48 yards).
13269.take: The rookie's debut is pushed back by at least a week, and the coaching staff is backing Cousins publicly despite the losing streak. A switch still looks likely at some point this season if the Raiders keep losing, but nobody can predict when. He has no redraft value in 1QB leagues until he is named the starter. In superflex dynasty, the No. 1 overall pick is a long-term QB for a rebuilding team, and this delay may lower his price a little, so it's a good moment to buy.

9221.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
9221.headline: New shoulder injury kept Gibbs out Wednesday; Vikings game uncertain
9221.news: Gibbs did not practice Wednesday, Oct 28, because of a shoulder injury that had not been disclosed before, and the team did not call it a rest day. If he plays, start him as an RB1 even against a tough Vikings front, because the workload is unmatched. If he sits, Vaki and Saylors would split a bad matchup and neither is a reliable flex. In dynasty he's a 24-year-old cornerstone, and even a 1-5 rebuilder should hold rather than sell at a discount while he's banged up.

12519.headline: Led Bears with 4-130-1 in TNF win over Patriots

In redraft he's a WR3/flex with upside, and Chicago's next game isn't until Nov 2. In dynasty, his price just jumped, but a second-year receiver with this playmaking ability and Williams at QB is still worth buying.

With Burrow throwing well, Higgins is a reliable WR2 who can post WR1 weeks, and on this day he outproduced Ja'Marr Chase. In redraft he's a weekly start, and his price has now gone up, so the buy-low window is mostly closed. In dynasty he's in his prime on a long-term deal with a healthy QB, which makes him a stable hold rather than a sell-high.

Drake Maye threw for 321 yards and three TDs in the loss, and A.J. Brown also had a quiet night. The Patriots had extra rest and play at Miami on Sunday, Nov 1.
9501.take: The drop to four targets in Week 7 is a concern because his opportunities shrank even with Doubs and Hollins out, and his touchdown run was always going to cool off. He still projects as the No. 2 option next to Brown in an offense with a productive QB. Miami's defense is a good matchup, so he's a reasonable WR3/flex in 12-team leagues. In dynasty he's a smaller slot receiver on a modest contract with a capped ceiling, so if anyone is still paying for the two-game spike, take a pick for him.

4993.name: Mike Gesicki
4993.headline: Erick All to IR with feared ACL tear, boosting Gesicki
4993.news: Gesicki caught his only target for a 6-yard touchdown in the Oct 25 win at Baltimore, his fifth TD of the season. On Oct 27 the Bengals placed Erick All Jr. on injured reserve with a feared torn right ACL, suffered in the third quarter of that game, and signed TE Cam Grandy off the Vikings' practice squad. With All and Tanner Hudson on IR, the tight ends are Gesicki (the slot/receiving TE), blocker Drew Sample, Grandy, and rookie Jack Endries, who is expected to see more work. Cincinnati hosts Tennessee in Week 8.
4993.take: All's injury takes away Gesicki's main rival for receiving-TE snaps, so his routes should rise from the part-time level he's been at. Even so, he has averaged about three targets a game, and his fantasy points have come almost entirely from touchdowns, which rarely stay that frequent. The home game against Tennessee makes him a reasonable Week 8 TE streamer. In dynasty a 31-year-old has no place on a 1-5 rebuilder, so sell him to a contender while the touchdowns and the bigger role hold up his price.

11563.name: Bo Nix
11563.headline: Record 62-yard TD run powers Broncos past Cardinals
11563.news: Nix went 15-of-29 for 222 yards and one TD and ran 7 times for 73 yards and a TD in Denver's 30-16 win at Arizona on Oct 25. His 62-yard TD run broke Tim Tebow's record for the longest by a Broncos QB. He also threw a 52-yard screen TD to RJ Harvey, and he had no turnovers. Coverage noted concerns about Denver's offense after six weeks, but the Broncos are now 5-2 with three straight wins. They face the Chiefs in Week 8.
11563.take: His passing volume is modest, but rushing upside like this lifts his fantasy floor and ceiling, so he's a QB1 in 1QB leagues. Kansas City is a tougher matchup, but his legs keep him startable. In superflex dynasty he's a young starter on a winning team, which is exactly what a 1-5 rebuilder needs. Buy him if a contender values him like a mid-tier QB2.

11834.name: Devaughn Vele
11834.headline: Every-down role and a Paris touchdown; Saints on bye
11834.news: Vele caught 5 passes for 54 yards and scored on a 1-yard throw from Tyler Shough in New Orleans' 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh in Paris on Oct. 25. He led the Saints' receivers with a 92% snap share in that game, and Shough finished 30 of 38 for 278 yards. The Saints dropped to 2-5. New Orleans is on bye in Week 8, and its next game is Nov. 8 at home against Cleveland.
11834.take: A 92% snap share means he's a full-time starter, and Shough's high-volume, short-area passing suits his possession style. The problem is the ceiling: the Saints are a low-scoring 2-5 offense, and his production has been steady rather than spiky. With the bye, there's no reason to roster him in 12-team redraft this week, though he's a reasonable watch-list player for Week 9. In dynasty he's a useful depth receiver on a cheap profile, but not a long-term core piece for a rebuild, so hold him or move him as a throw-in.

3214.name: Hunter Henry

Miami is a decent matchup, which makes him a solid streaming starter in 12-team redraft if your tight end is on bye or struggling. In dynasty he's a veteran in his 30s with little long-term value, so a rebuilding team should sell him to a contender while his numbers are good.

11655.name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
11655.headline: Hamstring lands Tracy on IR; earliest return Week 13
11655.news: Tracy ran 6 times for 15 yards and a touchdown before hurting his left hamstring in the first half of the Giants' 27-21 overtime win at Houston on Oct 25. New York placed him on injured reserve on Oct 27, and GM Joe Schoen said the injury isn't season-ending or long-term. Because the Week 8 bye doesn't count toward the four-game minimum, reports put his earliest return at the Dec 6 home game against San Francisco. The Giants signed rookie RB Gregory Desrosiers off the Chargers' practice squad. Cam Skattebo, who ran for a career-high 124 yards in Week 7, now leads the backfield with Devin Singletary behind him.
11655.take: Even in a best case Tracy misses about a month of games, and he returns behind Skattebo, who just had his best game. That leaves Tracy with little redraft value until December, so in a 12-team league he's a drop candidate unless you have an IR slot. In dynasty he's a mid-20s backup on a Day 3 profile, which doesn't fit a rebuild; move him for any small return, though his value right now is low.

13276.name: Omar Cooper Jr.
13276.headline: Rookie posts second straight 100-yard game; top waiver add
13276.news: Cooper caught 5 passes for 115 yards and a TD in the Jets' 28-25 loss to Miami on Oct 25, including a 52-yard catch that set up another score. That made him the first rookie in franchise history with 100-plus yards in back-to-back games, after a 100-yard game against New England in Week 6 (218 yards over the two weeks). He played well even with Adonai Mitchell back from injury. He spent early-season time on IR with an ankle injury from Week 1. RotoBaller called him a must-add for Week 8, and ClutchPoints ranked him its No. 1 pickup with 34.7% rostered. The Jets host the Raiders on Sunday, Nov 1.
13276.take: Two straight games with 5+ targets, 100+ yards and a TD is a real breakout, and he is producing alongside Garrett Wilson and Mitchell rather than only because others were hurt. With five catches a game the volume is still modest, so his yards per catch will come down, but his role looks secure. He is a strong WR3/flex in redraft against a struggling Raiders team. In dynasty, a productive rookie fits a rebuilding team well, and his price will only rise if he keeps this up, so buy now if a manager will move him for a modest pick.

13424.name: Seth McGowan
13424.headline: Career-high 11 carries as Taylor's backup; deep stash
13424.news: In Indianapolis' 16-10 loss to Minnesota on Oct 25, McGowan ran 11 times for 46 yards and caught his only target for 2 yards, both career highs for carries and rushing yards. He played a season-high share of the snaps. Reports put that share at 31% to 34.5%. He also had 140 kick-return yards. Jonathan Taylor still led the backfield with 18 carries for 95 yards and a TD. Through seven games McGowan has 34 carries for 134 yards, 4 catches for 12 yards, and 566 kick-return yards. RotoBaller called him a priority stash before the trade deadline.
13424.take: McGowan is clearly Taylor's backup and got more work in Week 7, but without an injury to Taylor he isn't a standalone start, since he is averaging 3.9 yards per carry. His value comes from being the next man up behind a workhorse, which matters most to Taylor managers and in deep leagues. For a rebuilding dynasty team he is a cheap flier: a seventh-round rookie with a clear role, so he's worth adding if a bench spot is open, but don't pay to get him.
